items.title: Calculating Average Rate of Change Between Two Dates

sections.normalized_html:
The scatterplot shows the relationship between the time [MATH: y,] in hours, that a tagged owl spent in nocturnal flight, and the number of days, [MATH: x,] after September [MATH: 1.]

What is the average rate of change, in hours per day, of the length of time the owl spent in nocturnal flight from September [MATH: 3] to September [MATH: 8?]
sections.readable_text:
The scatterplot shows the relationship between the time [MATH: y,] in hours, that a tagged owl spent in nocturnal flight, and the number of days, [MATH: x,] after September [MATH: 1.]

[IMG: /graphics/e3fb039629474d92f636e00756fdbd9f]

What is the average rate of change, in hours per day, of the length of time the owl spent in nocturnal flight from September [MATH: 3] to September [MATH: 8?]

sections.normalized_html:
For the graph shown, [MATH: x] represents the number of days (after September [MATH: 1]) and [MATH: y] represents the time in hours. Therefore, the average rate of change, in hours per day, of the number of hours that the tagged owl spent in nocturnal flight between two [MATH: x]-values is the difference in the corresponding [MATH: y]-values divided by the difference between the [MATH: x]-values.

Since the [MATH: x]-values represent the days after September [MATH: 1,] the origin at [MATH: x = 0] corresponds to that date.

Now, we convert the dates September [MATH: 3] and September [MATH: 8] into [MATH: x]-values.

  • September [MATH: 3] corresponds to [MATH: x = 2.]

  • September [MATH: 8] corresponds to [MATH: x = 7.]

Notice that the graph shows that at [MATH: x = 2,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: 14.] Similarly, the graph shows that at [MATH: x = 7,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: 9.]

Therefore, the average rate of change from [MATH: x = 2] to [MATH: x = 7] (from September [MATH: 3] to September [MATH: 8]) is [MATH: \frac{9-14}{7-2} = \frac{-5}{5} = -1\,\text{hour per day}.]
